brief:
Reconstruction efforts in Gaza confront severe obstacles as the enclave lacks adequate medical professionals capable of treating complex war-related deformities, the Ma'an news agency reported. Hospitals struggle with limited surgical capacity and insufficient expertise to address the range of injuries inflicted during armed conflict, leaving many patients without access to reconstructive care.

The shortage reflects broader healthcare collapse across Gaza, where infrastructure damage and mass displacement have depleted the medical workforce. Patients requiring specialized orthopedic and plastic surgery procedures face long delays or must seek treatment abroad, options unavailable to most due to the blockade and economic hardship.
title: Gaza faces acute shortage of specialists to treat war injuries
